findings: The stationary cable tower changes construction, width, pulley geometry and base footprint between frames in both sequences. Female frame 0 has a single cropped upright while subsequent frames introduce different multi-upright/weight-stack assemblies. Male frame 1 has a broad curved base unlike frames 0, 2 and 3. These are conspicuous equipment morphs unrelated to pulling motion, materially disrupting animation.

Jagged dark horizontal remnants extend inward from both shoes with abrupt cut edges and speckling. They differ from the smoother ground shadows in other frames and are visible especially on the light background.

Female clothing changes across the ordered sequence: frames 0 and 3 have calf-length leggings, while frames 1 and 2 have ankle-length leggings; frame 2 also replaces the exposed central abdomen with a dark shirt-like panel. These conspicuous changes create outfit flicker unrelated to walking.

Opaque pale gray patches surround shoes and bench feet, most conspicuously in both frame-2 images; these read as leftover ground/background on dark surfaces. Smaller but clear patches also occur in male 1 and female 0/3.

Stationary bench construction and perspective change across frames: support spacing, crossbar visibility and bench width vary. Feet and seated orientation shift with the redraws, especially male 2 and female 1/2, beyond the finger motion. This causes obvious scene jumps despite broadly consistent body scale and identity.
Large opaque pale floor-shaped patch below the bench, with white residue around shoes and tower bases.
Ragged white residue and detached speckles below the bench and around shoes and tower bases.
Large baked white/gray checkerboard patch below the bench and white residue around shoes and tower bases.
Large baked white/gray checkerboard patch below the bench and white residue around shoes and tower bases.
Limited white fringe around bench supports, shoes and tower bases.

The stationary bench changes markedly in length, height, position and support geometry: frames 1–2 have a much larger bench than 0 and 3, and the legs alternate between straight and splayed designs. This produces obvious equipment/athlete scale jumps independent of the intended knee movement.

The stationary bench changes length, height and leg design across the sequence. Frame 2 has notably taller supports and a larger bench, while frame 3 has a much shorter bench and different feet. These stationary equipment changes create visible jumps beyond the intended leg and torso motion.

In both ordered sequences the stationary bench shifts downward and horizontally as the legs rise; its length, leg angles, and support geometry also change. Male frame 0 has a much shorter bench with upright posts, frame 1 expands it markedly, and later frames reposition it. Female frame 3 introduces diagonal braces absent from earlier frames. The athlete's head and torso drift with the bench. These are substantial stationary-anchor/equipment changes beyond the intended leg-raise motion and would visibly jump during animation.

The stationary incline bench is redrawn with changing support geometry and floor-base positions across each sequence. Male frame 1 has a rounded front crossbar unlike the rectangular bars in other frames; female frame 1 introduces a side handle absent in the other frames, and frame 0 has a differently placed front floor foot. These changes cause visible equipment morphing during the curl sequence.
Male dumbbell plates change from faceted in frame 0 to round in frame 1 and back to faceted in later frames; this is not explained by the curl movement alone.

In both sequences the ankle restraint and planted shoes translate markedly left and upward from the upright setup to the lowered pose, then shift again on return. This is visible on equal-canvas sequence sheets and is separate from the intended torso rotation; the floor anchor should remain stationary. The jump materially disrupts animation continuity.

Both setup frames retain a conspicuous pale gray oval floor/shadow patch that disappears in subsequent frames. It is especially bright on dark backgrounds; the female patch has ragged transparent breaks along its right edge. This may originate as an authored shadow, but its inconsistent presence and pale fill warrant cleanup review.

A thin pale fringe is visible along portions of the outer silhouette and restraint on dark backgrounds. The illustration remains readable; this is a limited edge artifact rather than an opaque background.

Female barbell is substantially longer in frame 0 than frames 1–3, and sleeve/plate perspective switches between frames 1 and 2. This is not explained by the vertical press and produces visible equipment morphing.

The grounded body shifts vertically across both sequences: head, torso and shoes rise in middle frames then drop on return. Male head also moves left and changes viewing angle from frame 0 to later frames. These stationary-anchor and viewpoint changes would cause obvious animation drift beyond the intended arm/bar motion.

Female top exposes a waist strip in frames 0 and 3 but becomes a longer continuous top in frames 1 and 2; shorts seam design also changes. Athlete remains recognizable, but clothing morphs through the sequence.

Male frame 0 places hips, head and planted feet substantially lower than frames 1–2; frame 3 only partly returns to that placement. The body pitch and apparent bar/plate size also change. These shifts exceed the arm/bar movement of the press and will cause a conspicuous body jump in the ordered sequence.

A thin pale fringe and scattered light edge pixels outline portions of the skin, clothing, hair and equipment against the dark background. No large opaque background or enclosed checkerboard patch was observed.

Female feet, hips and head move slightly between drawings, especially frame 0 versus the lowered positions. Less pronounced than the male sequence, but the stationary silhouette does not remain fully anchored.

The stationary mat changes length/shape and vertical position between frames in both sequences. Male frame 2 sits visibly lower than frame 3, and female frames 1-2 sit lower than 0/3. The mat also lengthens substantially from frame 0 to frame 1. These changes move the supported torso/hand contact line and cause visible animation jumping beyond the intended leg movement.

A continuous opaque pale/white strip with visible checker-like blocks runs beneath the sled and between the feet in every frame. It is especially conspicuous on the dark background and is separate from the intended shoe soles and sled rails.
Thin pale edging remains around portions of the athlete, hair, and equipment, visible against the dark background.

Frame 0 in both sequences places the foot/sled ground line lower than frames 1–3, causing a modest vertical jump at the loop boundary. The changing stride and torso angle themselves are plausible exercise movement.

Both sequences enlarge the athlete and barbell substantially from standing frame 0 through squat frames 1 and 2, then shrink in frame 3. Plate diameters, bar span and head size grow while head and feet remain near the same canvas edges. This is a zoom/scale change beyond genuine squat motion and will cause visible pulsing in animation.

Male torso markings change substantially: frame 0 has red central abdominal panels, frame 1 only a small lower red patch, frame 2 a broad red abdomen, and frame 3 a black central abdomen with red side and shoulder panels. These changes visibly flicker across the sequence.
Thin pale fringe follows portions of the athlete silhouette and ground-shadow perimeter on dark backgrounds; light backgrounds largely hide it.

Female frame 1 has a visibly enlarged head, torso and limb thickness relative to the standing and airborne frames, and is bulkier than the other squat frame. The change in body-part scale exceeds the expected change from bending into a squat and creates a noticeable size pop in the sequence.
Ground-shadow baseline shifts upward in squat frames relative to setup/jump frames in both sequences. Airborne foot elevation is appropriate, but the floor position itself also moves modestly.

Opaque white/light checker-pattern patches remain in enclosed gaps between the bent arms, head and shoulders in every frame. Frame 0 of both genders also has a broad light-gray/white region beneath the body and between the legs; frame 3 retains a white leg gap. These remain light on the dark preview rather than revealing the background.

Male frame 3 abruptly loses the shoes and shows bare toes, circular knee/elbow joint outlines and segmented mannequin-like limbs. Frame 0 uses more detailed realistic shading and footwear than the simplified later frames; hair shape also changes. This creates an obvious appearance discontinuity.

Both sequences change from an oblique reclining view to a frontal upright view and back, with the feet shifting substantially horizontally despite remaining together on the floor. Female frame 1 also raises the foot baseline relative to adjacent frames. Torso elevation is expected movement, but the viewpoint/foot anchoring changes make the animation inconsistent.
A thin light fringe traces portions of the outer silhouette and shadow on the dark background.

The stationary box moves substantially horizontally between frames, especially male 0 to 2, and changes width/perspective. The female box also visibly shrinks from setup to takeoff and changes position and perspective at landing. These changes would make the equipment jump in animation independently of the athlete's legitimate motion.
A small opaque white wedge remains in the gap between the forearms near the wrists in female frame 2, conspicuous against the dark background.

Thin intermittent greenish/light edge speckles follow portions of hair, body and box contours, most apparent around the female setup frame on dark. Limited fringe rather than a large opaque background.

In both sequences the hurdle changes construction: frame 0 has a narrow low U-shaped obstacle, frame 1 a wider tubular training hurdle, frame 2 a much wider bar on tall cone supports, and frame 3 a low hurdle again. These are conspicuous equipment shape and size changes rather than athlete movement.

Both athletes have markedly smaller heads and torsos in the front-facing overhead-arm setup (frame 0) than in frames 1-3. The body is enlarged as the pose compresses and the view changes to three-quarter, creating an apparent zoom through the hop. Genuine knee flexion and airborne displacement do not explain the head and torso size change.

White/light-gray retained background fills the enclosed gaps between both arms and torso. The patches remain light on the dark composite, with checkerboard texture visible especially in female frame 0, so these are not transparent gaps or garment highlights.
Thin pale dotted fringe traces portions of hair, arms, legs and shoes on the dark composites. Limited perimeter residue; figures remain usable.

Thin pale contour fringe remains visible against dark backgrounds on the athlete and barbell. Female frame 0 additionally has detached pale flecks near the right weight plate and body/bar edges. Limited artifacts; no opaque background, substantial interior remnants, or large missing regions.

Thin pale, intermittently jagged fringe is visible around hair, body and equipment contours against the dark background. It is limited to edges, with no substantial background residue or unwanted interior holes.

Bench support/base geometry and position vary slightly across phases, especially between frame 0 and later frames. Feet also shift modestly. The sequence remains readable and the arm raise itself is intentional movement.

Thin pale/gray fringe follows portions of the hair, clothing, limbs and equipment contours on dark backgrounds. It is limited to edges; no substantial opaque interiors, checkerboards or detached residue were observed.

Thin pale outlines and scattered light edge flecks remain around the cutouts, especially male limbs/clothing and female hair/equipment. Visible on dark backgrounds; no substantial opaque background, interior holes, clipping, or broken anatomy observed.

Thin pale, intermittently speckled edge fringe is visible on dark backgrounds around portions of the hair, arms and equipment contours. It is limited to the perimeter; there is no substantial opaque background or interior checkerboard.

Thin pale outlines are visible against the dark background around portions of rack/bench edges and athlete contours; especially female ponytail tips. Limited fringe, not a substantial opaque background.

Stationary rack, bench and planted-foot positions drift slightly between frames, with small changes to rack hooks and bench geometry. This is separate from the intended vertical bar/arm motion; movement remains readable.

Thin pale fringes trace portions of the athlete outline on dark backgrounds, most visible around female ponytails and male shoulders/shorts. No substantial opaque interior background or missing clothing regions observed.

Male rack varies slightly across frames, especially frame 3: the left post/bar top rises and the post shifts left relative to frames 1–2, despite the base remaining at a similar height. This introduces limited equipment jitter independent of the rowing motion.
A thin detached vertical pale streak is visible near the upper-left canvas edge, separate from the athlete and mat.

Thin pale edge fringes are visible on dark backgrounds around portions of the figures and mat. Female frame 1 has the most conspicuous bright strip beneath the mat; other frames show narrower intermittent outlines. Artwork remains usable.

Male frame 0 has a narrower mat and its feet sit farther right than in frames 1–3, creating a limited stationary-anchor shift when transitioning into the bridge. This is distinct from expected hip elevation.

Thin pale fringe appears around portions of athlete and equipment on dark backgrounds. Female frame 1 has the clearest scattered light flecks along tower edges, cables, bench and shoe; female frame 2 and male frame 1 have small pale strips beneath tower bases. No broad opaque background or checkerboard interior is visible.

Tower uprights, bench feet and planted shoes shift modestly between frames, most visibly female frame 1 relative to 0/2 and male frame 2 relative to 0/1. These are stationary-anchor changes in addition to intended arm movement; overall scale and identity remain recognizable.
Thin cable has visible interruptions between the stopper and pulley, strongest in male frame 0. The handle and pulley remain recognizable; this is a limited line defect.

Small changes in face rendering, torso contours and foot positions accompany the arm movement. Female frame 2 lowers the head relative to frames 1 and 3 while the feet and pulley remain largely fixed. Limited drift, without a large scale or identity change.

Irregular white/gray strips or flecks remain just below the pulley projection/base in all frames. Female frames also retain a white patch between the ponytail bottom and mat. These are localized exterior residue, not a full opaque background.

The stationary blue mat progressively widens and athlete framing grows somewhat between frames 0 and 3 in both sequences; pulley position also shifts slightly. The modest variation is separate from the intended knee/hip motion and may produce a small animation pulse.

Thin pale, intermittently speckled contour fringe is visible against the dark background, particularly around hair, shoulders, limbs and equipment. No broad opaque background or substantial enclosed residue is visible.

Female frame 0 places both pulley bases visibly higher than frames 1–3; the bench base also shifts slightly downward after frame 0 while shoes remain near the same baseline. This produces limited equipment jitter beyond the intended arm movement.
